top_note.title: Prop. 37 is still projected to pass.
top_note.body:
The count grew overnight and the margin held. The Secretary of State's semi-official tally as of 7:20 PM PT Wednesday has Prop. 37, the loan program for middle income buyers of newly built homes, at 61.2% Yes (4,783,474 votes) to 38.8% No (3,036,774), about 268,000 more ballots than Wednesday morning. Alameda County is at 67.5% Yes.

Mail ballots postmarked by Election Day still count if they arrive within seven days, and the state certifies the result by Dec. 11.

image.alt: Prop. 37 results chart: California statewide Yes 61.2% (4,783,474 votes) to No 38.8% (3,036,774), semi-official count as of 7:20 PM PT Nov. 4, 2026; Bay Area counties Yes: San Francisco 71.8%, Alameda 67.5%, San Mateo 65.4%, Contra Costa 64.6%, Santa Clara 61.2%

top_note.source: Source: California Secretary of State, semi-official results.

real_estate.homebuilder: Rates hold at 7.22%, and Zillow says higher than expected rates cooled home sales.
real_estate.commentary:
Mortgage News Daily's 30-year average is 7.22% this morning, unchanged, and the 15-year is 6.86%, up 0.01. Rates kept easing after our Wednesday report went out: the 30-year finished Wednesday at 7.22%, not the 7.25% we printed that morning. At 7.22%, a Fremont buyer at today's $1,299,444 median with 20% down would pay about $7,070 a month in principal and interest, $57 less than at Tuesday's 7.30%.

Zillow said the same thing from the other side of the table. Its residential revenue, mostly fees from real estate agents, fell 4% from a year ago to $419 million, which it blamed on higher than expected mortgage rates slowing sales, while rentals grew 26%. Most of its $158 million loss was a $165 million settlement of a shareholder lawsuit over Zillow Offers, its old home buying business. The stock rose 9.43% Wednesday before the report and is down 9.0% this morning.

The board wide table is 2,443, from 2,438 Wednesday, with 149 coming soon and 129 brand new. The five city ledger is 634, from 642: Fremont (214) fell four, Milpitas (97) three, Hayward (181) and Union City (60) one each, and Newark (82) added one.

What this means for you: stocks are falling and the 10-Year is easing this morning, and that tends to reach lender rate sheets within a day. If you are close to locking, ask your lender to watch it with you rather than guess. Sellers, 171 homes in our five cities have been listed 60 days or longer; the market is rewarding the right price, not the hopeful one.

• Board wide: 2,443 listings across our 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, with 149 coming soon and 129 brand new.

📍 Alameda County (Fremont Focus)

• Live ledger: 634 listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City. 567 are on the market and 67 are coming soon.
• Fremont: 214 live, 163 active, 30 coming soon, 20 brand new and 1 back on the market. The median on market list price is $1,299,444 at $814 a square foot, and the typical active listing has been out 36 days.
• The rest of the ledger: Hayward 181, Milpitas 97, Newark 82, Union City 60.
• Across all five cities the median is $1,049,000 at $667 a square foot. 276 homes are priced under a million, and 171 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

stocks.note: Levels are Wednesday, November 4 at the closing bell. Live at 8:55 AM PT Thursday: Dow down 2.36%, S&P 500 down 3.18%, Nasdaq down 4.31%.
stocks.news:
Wednesday's rally is coming undone. As of 8:55 AM PT the Nasdaq is down 4.31%, the S&P 500 down 3.18% and the Dow down 2.36%, led by a selloff in chip and AI stocks: the Philadelphia semiconductor index is down 9.3%. Qualcomm, down 11.3%, reported results after Wednesday's close. Wednesday, the morning after Election Day, the Dow had jumped 3.03% and the S&P 500 1.58%. One day's rally, one day's refund.

The memory chip boom shows up plainly in South Korea (chart). Its current account surplus hit a record $61.5 billion in September, 4.3 times a year earlier, as goods exports reached $130.7 billion, and the first nine months already total $340.7 billion against $123.1 billion for all of 2025. Samsung and SK hynix, both with U.S. headquarters in San Jose, make most of those chips. Korea's Kospi fell 5.3% Thursday as the selloff spread.

feature_image.caption: South Korea's current account surplus hit a record $61.5 billion in September, 4.3 times a year earlier, on memory chip exports.
feature_image.source: Bank of Korea, balance of payments (ECOS), through September 2026

economy.note: Levels are Wednesday, November 4: the 10-Year is Treasury's close, gold and silver are COMEX December settlements, and Brent is the ICE January settlement. Live at 8:55 AM PT Thursday: 10-Year 4.83%, gold $4,131.00 (+1.42%), silver $52.77 (+0.94%), Brent $96.85 (+2.36%).
economy.commentary:
Private employers added 86,000 jobs in October, ADP reported Wednesday, a second solid month, though professional and business services lost 27,000, a third monthly decline in a row. The government's own October jobs report is due Friday.

ADP does not allow charts built from its data, so we drew the local version from public BLS figures (chart). Over the year to September, the San Jose metro added 19,900 private jobs, 11,100 of them in education and health, while the East Bay, home to Fremont, Hayward, Newark and Union City, lost 5,700, led by manufacturing (down 5,100) and construction (down 4,400). Education and health led the gains on both sides of the Bay.

Oil fell hard Wednesday. Brent settled at $94.62, down 8.67% and back under $100, on hopes the Iran war winds down sooner; it is up 2.36% this morning near $96.85. Gold settled up 3.37% and silver 5.08%. Two corrections: Market Briefs stamped gold at $4,145 (+1.78%) and Brent at $93.62 (-1.06%) as Wednesday's 4 PM ET levels, but both were Thursday's overnight prices measured against Wednesday's settlements, a fourth day running, and Treasury has the 10-Year closing Wednesday at 4.90%, down 0.05, not 4.85%.

feature_image.alt: Paired bar chart of private sector job change by industry, September 2025 to September 2026. East Bay (Oakland-Fremont-Berkeley, Alameda and Contra Costa counties) total down 5,700: education and health up 5,100, leisure and hospitality up 1,900, trade transport and utilities up 2,000, other services up 800, construction and mining down 4,400, professional and business down 2,100, financial down 1,700, manufacturing down 5,100, information down 2,200. San Jose metro total up 19,900: education and health up 11,100, leisure and hospitality up 2,500, trade up 1,100, other services up 200, construction and mining up 4,000, professional and business down 200, financial down 700, manufacturing up 2,600, information down 700
feature_image.caption: Over the year to September, the San Jose metro added 19,900 private jobs while the East Bay lost 5,700; education and health led the gains on both sides of the Bay.
feature_image.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Current Employment Statistics, State and Metro Area, not seasonally adjusted, September 2026 preliminary
